intended_object: The canonical K-algebra isomorphism between the coordinate ring of the upper-triangular subgroup T_n ⊆ GL_n (O(GL_n) modulo the entries below the diagonal) and the localization of the polynomial ring in the entries x_ij with i ≤ j at the restricted determinant, which is the product of the diagonal entries (Milne, Algebraic Groups, 2.40). This comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The library defines the coordinate ring as K[x_ij][1/det] modulo the ideal spanned by the x_ij with j < i. The preceding theorem shows that this ideal equals the generic `localizedCoordinateIdeal` for the retained set {(i,j) | ¬ j < i}, i.e. i ≤ j. The definition chains `Ideal.quotientEquivAlgOfEq` along that equality with the general isomorphism (K[σ]_f)/(X_i : i ∉ S) ≅ K[S]_{f|_{X_i=0, i∉S}}. Here `eraseCoordinates` is Mathlib's `killCompl`, which sets the erased variables to zero. So the target is K[x_ij : i ≤ j] localized at the determinant with the below-diagonal entries set to zero, i.e. at the product of the diagonal entries. That is exactly the standard presentation of O(T_n).

The setting (any commutative ring K, any finite linearly ordered index type) is the natural one: the generality is wider than Milne's field case, and the order is needed to say what "upper triangular" means. Mathlib has no such coordinate-ring presentation. The definition is an isomorphism that packages a theorem as data, but it is the canonical isomorphism and it is built correctly.
